title: HomeGuard Mold Remediation Containment Scope Guideline
content:
Containment of fungi, wet rot and bacteria remediation on a HomeGuard Homeowners Policy claim is scoped by the size of the visible mold and by whether the home has had an earlier paid water loss. The scope chosen sets the remediation figure on which the mold payment is built.

## Rule

Where the policy carries a payment entry for a water loss (sudden discharge, freeze, water backup or seepage) on another claim with a date of loss in the 36 months before the call and the mold replacement-cost value is at least 3000.00, the containment is extended over the whole wet area, because moisture from the earlier loss makes hidden growth beyond the visible mold likely, and the remediation figure is the recorded mold value plus 10 percent of the claim's dwelling water damage.

Where there is no such earlier paid water loss and the mold value is at least 3000.00, a single-area containment barrier is priced and the remediation figure is the recorded mold value plus 400.00.

Where the mold replacement-cost value is below 3000.00, no containment is priced and the remediation figure is the recorded mold value as estimated.

## Terms used in this guideline

- **Mold replacement-cost value (the recorded mold value):** the replacement-cost value recorded on the claim's repeated-seepage denial entry for the mold remediation.
- **The claim's dwelling water damage (the wet area):** the replacement-cost value on the claim's dwelling repeated-seepage denial entry together with that on any dwelling payment entry of the claim that replaces no denial.
- **Earlier paid water loss:** a payment entry on the same HomeGuard policy, on a claim other than the one being settled, whose cause of loss is a sudden and accidental discharge of water, a freeze, a water backup or repeated seepage and whose date of loss falls in the 36 months before the call.

## Scope table

| Earlier paid water loss in the 36 months before the call | Mold replacement-cost value | Containment scope | Remediation figure |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | 3000.00 or more | Whole wet area | Recorded mold value plus 10 percent of the claim's dwelling water damage |
| No | 3000.00 or more | Single-area barrier | Recorded mold value plus 400.00 |
| Yes | Below 3000.00 | None priced | Recorded mold value as estimated |
| No | Below 3000.00 | None priced | Recorded mold value as estimated |

A mold value of exactly 3000.00 is at least 3000.00 and falls on the priced rows; a value of 2999.99 is below it.

## Illustrations (hypothetical inputs only)

1. Recorded mold value 5000.00; dwelling repeated-seepage denial entry of 18000.00 and no dwelling payment entry that replaces no denial; a freeze claim paid on the policy with a date of loss 20 months before the call. Whole wet area: 10 percent of 18000.00 is 1800.00, and the remediation figure is 5000.00 plus 1800.00, that is 6800.00.
2. Same claim, but the earlier paid water claim has a date of loss 40 months before the call. It lies outside the 36 months, so the single-area barrier applies: 5000.00 plus 400.00, that is 5400.00.
3. Recorded mold value 3000.00, no earlier paid water loss: single-area barrier, 3400.00.
4. Recorded mold value 2400.00 with an earlier paid water loss inside the window: below 3000.00, so no containment is priced and the remediation figure stays 2400.00.
5. An earlier paid claim whose cause of loss was wind or hail is not a water loss and does not count as an earlier paid water loss.

## Q&A

**Does a payment on the claim being settled count as the earlier paid water loss?** No. Only a payment entry on another claim of the policy counts.

**What is measured when the wet area is used?** The replacement-cost value of the claim's dwelling water damage as defined above, not the mold value.

**Is the 400.00 barrier charge added when the whole wet area is contained?** No. The two scopes are alternatives: the whole-wet-area scope applies where an earlier paid water loss stands, the single-area barrier where none does.
